verses.1: He who loves his son will frequently chastise him, so that he may be happy in the very end, and not grope for the doors of his neighbors.
verses.2: He who instructs his son will be praised over him and will glory in him, in the midst of his household.
verses.3: He who teaches his son will make his enemy jealous, and in the midst of his friends, he will glory in him.
verses.4: When his father has died, it will be as if he were not dead. For he will have left behind someone who is like himself.
verses.5: In his life, he saw him and rejoiced in him. And at his passing, he was not sorrowful, nor was he confounded in the sight of his enemies.
verses.6: For he left behind himself a defender of his house against his enemies, and someone who will repay his friends with kindness.
verses.7: For the sake of the souls of his sons, he will bind up his wounds, and at every voice, his gut will be stirred up.
verses.8: An untamed horse becomes stubborn, and a child left to himself becomes headstrong.
verses.9: Coddle a son, and he will make you afraid. Play with him, and he will make you sorrowful.
verses.10: You should not laugh with him; otherwise you may have grief, and in the end, your teeth will be clenched.
verses.11: You should not give him power in his youth, but you should not despise his thoughts.
verses.12: Bow down his neck in his youth, and slap his sides while he is a child, lest perhaps he may become stubborn, and then he will not trust you, and so he will bring sorrow to your soul.
verses.13: Instruct your son, and work with him, lest you give offense by his shameful behavior.
verses.14: Better is a healthy pauper with a strong constitution, than a wealthy man who is weak and afflicted by maladies.
verses.15: A healthy soul with the sanctity of justice is better than all the gold and silver. And a sound body is better than immense revenues.
verses.16: There is no revenue above the revenue of a healthy body. And there is no delight above a joyful heart.
verses.17: Death is better than a bitter life. And eternal rest is better than continual sickness.
verses.18: Good things hidden in a closed mouth are like seats at a feast placed around a grave.
verses.19: What benefit is there in an offering to an idol? For it can neither eat, nor smell.
verses.20: So is he who flees from the Lord, carrying the wages of his iniquity.
verses.21: He sees with his eyes and groans, like a eunuch who embraces a virgin and sighs.
verses.22: You should not give your soul to sadness, and you should not afflict yourself by your own counsel.
verses.23: The gladness of the heart is the life of a man, and it is a treasure of sanctity without defect. And the exultation of a man is length of life.
verses.24: Take pity on your own soul by pleasing God, and show self-restraint. Gather your heart into his sanctity, and drive sadness far away from yourself.
verses.25: For sadness has killed many, and there is no usefulness in it.
verses.26: Envy and anger will diminish your days, and pensiveness will bring old age before its time.
verses.27: A cheerful and good heart is like a feast. And its feasts are formed by diligence. [ Sirach 31 ]
